edges.description: Represents a complaint status change event. Legacy unversioned edges exist in the immutable graph attached to collapsed legacy complaint vertices, so consumers must filter to `version = 2` to read only the corrected per-source-row status edges.
Records whether a debt belongs to a business treatment campaign at a business-effective time, preserving debt-level campaign lineage when a person has multiple debts.

Status transition edge from debt to dispute. Always query with `has('version', 2)` so legacy unversioned edges remaining in the immutable graph (e.g. resolved edges left over after a dispute's resolution_code was cleared in the source system) are ignored and the latest corrected status is used.

Represents a change in the forwarded status of a debt. IMPORTANT: consumers MUST filter to `version = 3` when traversing this edge. Earlier mapping generations (version 2 and unversioned legacy edges) do not carry the `vendor_type` discriminator and must be excluded.

Anchors a portal_session to the debt the consumer is interacting with. Producers emit this edge for every portal_session, including sessions originating from a short URL click and sessions started by direct navigation to the portal where no short_url or trace exists. The legacy short_url -> trace -> portal_session path remains valid for backward compatibility; this edge is the single durable anchor for discovering all portal sessions for a debt.
Directly attributes a text message to the debt whose account-level communication it records.

edges.deprecated_reason: Superseded for lawsuit modeling and debt.is_litigious indexing by debt_has_lawsuit. Historical negative events make this edge unsafe as the canonical current-state suppression source. It remains emitted only for legacy consumers such as claydol-agent; do not stop emission until those consumers migrate under a separate story.

edges.description: Links a debt rule exclusion event to the specific governed rule that caused the exclusion.
Links a debt rule exclusion event to the specific debt entity that was disqualified.
Links a debt rule exclusion event to the specific phone number that failed a phone-scoped rule.

Records that the phone-interactions eligibility filter marked this (debt, phone_number) pair as eligible to call on the day given by effective_at. One edge is emitted per debt-phone pair per daily eligibility run; presence with a given effective_at means the pair passed every phone-interactions rule on that day, so a rolling union of these edges over a window yields the set of calls we were allowed to place.

Self-loop attribution event on a payment that records which channel was assigned, which rule made the decision, and which source event supported it. The payment vertex remains immutable; current reporting values are derived from these edges.

Self edge on person carrying the person's date of birth as an immutable fact. Modeled as an edge instead of a person property so the durable person vertex stays minimal and the date-of-birth fact has its own lineage.
Records that a call associated with the phone number triggered the outbound text message. This attribution can be written before delayed phone_call edge ingestion completes.

edges.deprecated_reason: Replaced by person_phone_number_has_dnc which anchors the DNC event to both the person and the phone number, preventing cross-person DNC bleed when multiple persons share the same phone number.

Replaced by person_phone_number_status_changed which anchors the status change to both the person and the phone number, preventing cross-person status bleed when multiple persons share the same phone number.

edges.description: Links a portal_event to an experiment run the visitor was assigned to at the time of the event. Emitted per assignment: a single portal_event may have multiple portal_event_has_experiment edges when the visitor is concurrently assigned to more than one experiment run. The variant_key edge property records which variant of that experiment run was assigned for this portal_event.
Links a LOGIN_FAILED portal_event to its structured portal_login_failure record. Emitted only when the parent portal_event has event_type = LOGIN_FAILED.
Links a rule execution to the ruleset(s) evaluated during the run, recording sequence order when multiple rulesets are composed.
Associates a rule execution with the business treatment campaign under which it was evaluated.
Links a rule execution to an individual debt exclusion event recorded during that run.
Records lifecycle status transitions (STARTED, ENDED, COMPLETED, FAILED) and outcome metrics for a rule execution without mutating the stable execution vertex.
Associates the Rule product platform with a concrete execution run.
Associates the Rule product catalog with a governed ruleset.
Defines membership and sequence ordering of a governed rule within a ruleset.

Optional. Associates this settlement offer with a campaign context (for example, a Black Friday or pre-legal campaign offer). Presence marks the offer as belonging to the campaign; absence means the offer is not campaign-scoped.

Optional. Indicates this settlement offer is valid or offered through the linked company context (for example, an offer that can only be honored when the debt is being represented by a specific debt settlement agency, or a future offer context tied to another company role). The edge does not constrain the company's role  -  DSA-specific meaning is inferred when the same company is also linked to the debt via company_represents_debt with company_type = DEBT_SETTLEMENT_AGENCY. Optional and absent for offers that are not company-scoped.

vertices.description: Represents a physical or mailing address standardized according to USPS standards. Address data is saved to IPFS as part of the property information.
Represents an external asset referenced by a template, such as a Quiq-managed media asset.

Represents a balance record associated with a debt, tracking balance history over time. Always query balance vertices with has('version', 2) to avoid legacy balance vertices left in the immutable graph that stored balance_amount in raw cents (as integers) and date as epoch-millisecond integers; corrected balance vertices emitted by the current mapping are tagged with version=2 and store balance as a decimal dollar value with an ISO-8601 date string.
Represents a bankruptcy proceeding record.
Represents a distinct web browser identity (name + version) observed during a portal session. One vertex per (browser_name, browser_version) combination; deduped across sessions.

Represents a person-level calling-window observation derived from the latest consumer_contact source row for a debt. The observation carries the current state of the reported restriction: when `status` is true the observation is an active restriction with allowed_call_start_time / allowed_call_end_time meaningful for downstream scheduling; when `status` is false the source record cleared all restriction fields and any earlier active restriction MUST be treated as removed. Legacy observations persisted before `status` was introduced do not carry the property; downstream consumers MUST treat any calling_window_restriction lacking a `status` property as an active restriction (never as unrestricted) so calls to those consumers stay inside the persisted window until a fresh observation explicitly clears the restriction with `status = false`. Each incremental ingestion emits a fresh observation reflecting the latest source state so appearance and removal both flow through normal ingestion; deterministic business-effective ordering (effective_at, then created_at) is enforced on the linking person_has_calling_window_restriction edge. Day-window children linked via calling_window_restriction_has_day_window carry the SAME effective_at as the parent person→restriction edge for the observation batch that emitted them; day-window edges from earlier active observations that were later cleared or reactivated without day fields therefore have a stale effective_at and downstream Gremlin filters them out by matching the current parent-edge effective_at.
Represents a single allowed call window for a specific day of week within a person-level calling restriction.
Represents a business treatment campaign: a named, purpose-driven grouping of debts or people that should be treated differently for a period of time or business reason.

Represents overall call timing preferences tied to a phone number. This is a pure value object: identity is (phone_number, overall_call_start_time, overall_call_end_time[, calling_time_qualifier[, preferred_contact_notes]]). The business-effective timestamp of a given report lives on the incoming phone_number_has_communication_preference edge (and on the outgoing communication_preference_has_day_window edges) rather than on the vertex, so reports that observe the same overall window reuse a single vertex across runs. Two sources exist: (1) misc002 alpha-weight codes from demographic_phone, which are soft activity-weight signals; (2) consumer_contact records, which are hard compliance restrictions that must be respected.

Represents a preferred single call window for a specific day of week on a phone number. This is a stateless decomposition of the parent communication_preference vertex: identity is (phone_number, day_of_week, preferred_call_start_time, preferred_call_end_time). The business-effective timestamp lives on the parent communication_preference vertex; day-window vertices intentionally do not carry effective_at so that per-day fan-out remains stable across pipeline re-runs.
Represents a company or organization with basic information including name and contact details.

Represents a customer complaint record. Legacy unversioned complaint vertices exist in the immutable graph where multiple distinct source complaints collapsed into a single vertex; consumers must filter to `version = 2` to exclude them and query only corrected per-source-row complaint vertices.

Represents a court venue where a lawsuit was filed. Sourced from tlo_enrichment_info.lawsuit_history_court and shared across all lawsuits filed in the same court. Content-hashed on name so the graph store dedupes automatically across debts. A court_has_address edge to an address vertex may be added later if we start parsing city/state out of the raw TLO court label.
Represents one immutable daily business metric value persisted for a specific business date.

Represents one immutable channel and communication-type preference snapshot for a debt captured from the Payment Portal Preference Center. Each portal save emits a new debt_channel_preference vertex; the current preferences for a debt are the reached vertex with the newest effective_at.

Represents the customer-facing financial product associated with a debt (e.g., the credit card or loan brand the consumer recognizes, like "Indigo Mastercard" or "Best Egg"). Distinct from the legal original creditor (issuing company), which is linked via company_issues_debt_product.

Represents a discrete debt exclusion event occurring during a rule execution, capturing evaluation order, business-effective timestamp, and linking the excluded debt to the disqualifying rule (and candidate phone for phone-scoped rules).

Represents a distinct device class observed during a portal session (e.g., 'iPhone', 'iPad', 'Android Phone', 'Desktop'). One vertex per device_type value; deduped across sessions. This is a device class, not a per-device hardware identity.
Represents a dispute record on an account.
Represents a do-not-contact (DNC) status record.

Represents a do-not-email (DNE) status record for a person. DNE is email-only and is distinct from DNC, which restricts voice calls, and DNT, which restricts SMS. Sourced from the account-level account.do_not_email flag and modeled at the person level, so the opt-out applies to every email address the person owns rather than to a single address. The record is identified by person_identifier and status; the business-effective time of each transition lives on the person_has_dne edge.

Represents a do-not-text (DNT) status record for a person. DNT is SMS-only and is distinct from DNC, which restricts voice calls. Sourced from the account-level account.do_not_txt flag and modeled at the person level (one DNT record per primary debt's person).

Represents a specific launched run of a portal A/B experiment. Immutable: one vertex per experiment_run_id, and experiment_run_id always maps to the same experiment_key for that run. Portal events assigned to this experiment run are linked via the portal_event_has_experiment edge, which carries the assigned variant_key on the edge for each event.

Represents a single identifiable section inside a file, bounded by an inclusive 1-indexed page range. Applies to ANY file, not only MULTI_DOCUMENT composites: a single-purpose CONTRACT PDF can carry one file_content covering pages 1..N, or multiple file_content children for its distinct sections (Arbitration Agreement, ESIGN Consent, Credit Contract). The parent file is referenced via file_id so lineage survives the database's content-hash id override (child vertices carry their root identifier to avoid hash collisions). content_type is an independent, fine-grained enum that names the specific document form of each section  -  it is deliberately NOT mirrored from files.file_type, which is kept coarse.
Represents normalized metadata and additional properties associated with files, including statement classification, dates, agreements, and disclosures. Linked to files via relationship.
Represents a single stored file artifact with type classification and S3 source location.

Represents an approximate geolocation derived from an IP address or analytics client (city + region + country, with optional latitude/longitude). Distinct from the postal address vertex: this is non-postal, IP-derived location and does not require street-level fields. One vertex per (city_name, region, country_code) combination; deduped across sessions.
Represents an immutable income range enrichment associated with a person, sourced from the Credit Vision income band for a debt.
Represents a distinct IP address observed during a portal session. One vertex per ip_address value; deduped across sessions and consumers.
Represents a judgement awarded against a debt. Presence of this vertex on a debt indicates the debt has a judgement on file. Sourced from the legal_form table when judgment_date is populated.

Represents a lawsuit reported by TLO/TU on the tlo_enrichment_info table. One vertex per distinct court case (normalized case_number + normalized court_name), so the same real case referenced by multiple debts collapses to a single vertex - critical for CAFA class actions and serial-litigious plaintiff scenarios. Per-debt TLO enrichment metadata (match_score, match_count, distance, long_score, case_title, filing_date, cafa) lives on the debt_has_lawsuit edge, NOT on this vertex, so cross-debt duplicates dedupe cleanly and re-enrichment does not churn the vertex hash.

Represents a party named in a TLO lawsuit hit (plaintiff, defendant, attorney, judge, or law firm). Intentionally NOT typed as person or company: TLO gives raw comma-separated strings ('DENNIS E HENRY ATTORNEY', 'TRANS UNION LLC') that cannot be reliably classified and must not pollute the canonical person/company graph where identity matching happens. Role is expressed by the linking edge label (lawsuit_has_plaintiff / lawsuit_has_defendant / lawsuit_has_attorney / lawsuit_has_judge / lawsuit_has_lawfirm). Content-hashed on raw_name so identical names dedupe across lawsuits. Only emitted for TLO rows that would produce a lawsuit vertex (matches>=1 AND court populated), so no orphan parties are minted.

Represents a legal action / cause-of-action code cited in a TLO lawsuit (FDCPA, FCRA, TCPA, RESPA, BKPCY, STATE_XX, etc.). Sourced from tlo_enrichment_info.lawsuit_history_actions, which is a comma-separated string of these codes. One vertex per distinct code across the whole graph. Only emitted for TLO rows that would produce a lawsuit vertex (matches>=1 AND court populated), so no orphan actions are minted.
Seller-media package / drop container (e.g., Elevate Azure land) that groups related files or documents together; not merely a vague file batch.
Represents a distinct operating system identity (name + version) observed during a portal session. One vertex per (os_name, os_version) combination; deduped across sessions.

Represents a real money event applied to a debt. One vertex per actual money event (received). May or may not be linked to a payment_plan or to a specific payment_plan_installment. Reversals/NSF/chargebacks/voids are modeled as payment_status_changed edges on the original payment, not as separate payment vertices.
Represents a payment arrangement record.

Represents a single scheduled slot within a payment plan: the planned charge for one date in the plan's schedule (scheduled_amount, payment_method). Independent of whether money was actually received, and independent of whether a payment attempt exists: slots are created both from attempted payments and, for already-booked future obligations with no payment row yet, from the authoritative payment_plan_schedule row (ownership resolved through payment_plan, which is the only place debt_id lives). Lifecycle (SCHEDULED, PAID, FAILED, CANCELLED, RESCHEDULED, COMPLETED) and the scheduled date for the slot are recorded on payment_plan_installment_status_changed edges; the latest scheduled date and latest lifecycle state are projected onto this vertex by the scheduled_payment_date and installment_status_latest derived indexes. The owning plan is always reachable through payment_plan_has_installment. When a real money event satisfies a slot, a payment_plan_installment_has_payment edge links the installment to its payment.
Represents an individual person with basic personal information including name and contact details.

Represents an immutable language-preference value object for a person. Version changes over time are captured as new person_has_language_preference edges (which carry the business-effective timestamp), not as new vertex snapshots; identical (person_identifier, preferred_language) pairs dedupe forever.

Represents an individual phone call attempt. Only immutable identity facts live on the vertex (with direction present when derivable from source_type); observations that arrive after the call is initiated (lifecycle status, contact type reached, transcript, sentiment, AI outputs) are modeled through subsequent edges. Linked to the dialed consumer phone_number via phone_number_has_phone_call, to the phone_number that originated the call via phone_number_originated_phone_call, to the debt context via debt_has_phone_call, to the specific person reached via person_has_phone_call, to lifecycle status transitions via phone_call_status_changed (self edges), to the contact type classification via phone_call_contact_identified (self edges), to sentiment observations via phone_call_sentiment_assessed (self edges), to AI response scores via phone_call_ai_response_scored (self edges), to the transcript artifact via phone_call_has_transcript_artifact_uri (self edge), to per-call compliance observations via phone_call_compliance_event (self edges). Replaces the prior edge-based phone_call model; the phone_call edge type is retained for backward compatibility.
Represents an immutable phone contactability profile derived from PBI-style contactability attributes.
Represents an immutable phone verification result with verification state and name-to-phone linkage outcome.

Represents a single discrete event observed in the consumer-facing debt portal during a portal session: landing on a page, a login outcome, or downstream payment/plan actions taken from a settlement offer (method selection, payment-details entry, payment-plan-details entry, authorization submission, authorization success, payment made, plan created, good faith offer selection). Each event is immutable; one vertex per distinct portal event. Browser, operating system, device, IP, and geolocation are session-level and are linked from the parent portal_session rather than being duplicated on each event. When event_type is LOGIN_FAILED, the structured failure reason and any sanitized detail are linked from a separate portal_login_failure vertex via the portal_event_has_login_failure edge rather than carried as properties on this vertex. When the payment-related event references a known scheduled installment slot (typically PAYMENT_METHOD_SELECTED, PAYMENT_DETAILS_ENTERED, PAYMENT_AUTHORIZATION_SUBMITTED, PAYMENT_AUTHORIZED, PAYMENT_MADE), it is linked to the existing payment vertex via the portal_event_has_payment edge; the selected payment method is carried by the payment vertex's payment_method property rather than duplicated on the portal_event.

Represents the structured failure reason for a single LOGIN_FAILED portal_event in the consumer-facing debt portal. One vertex per LOGIN_FAILED event (per-event record, not a deduped lookup). Linked from its parent portal_event via the portal_event_has_login_failure edge. Only emitted when the parent portal_event has event_type = LOGIN_FAILED.

Represents a single browser session in the consumer-facing debt portal. Groups one or more portal_event vertices that occurred within the same session. Session-level environment attributes (browser, operating_system, device, ip_address, geolocation) are linked from this vertex rather than duplicated on each event. Every portal_session is anchored to its debt via the debt_has_portal_session edge so sessions are discoverable from the debt regardless of how the consumer reached the portal. A portal_session may additionally be reachable from one or more trace vertices when the consumer opens a short URL within the same browser session; sessions started from direct portal navigation (no short URL click) have no trace path and are reached exclusively through debt_has_portal_session.
Represents a portfolio of debt owned by a company (seller).

Represents a physical postal mail piece sent to a person. Linked to the recipient via person_has_postal_mail, to the owning debt via debt_has_postal_mail, to the delivery address via postal_mail_has_address, to the campaign it belongs to via postal_mail_has_mail_campaign, and to lifecycle status transitions via postal_mail_status_changed (self edges).

Represents one immutable, source-scoped alternative requirement group. A dispute requirement group is satisfied when any linked required_document alternative matches a debt file. Separate groups and direct ungrouped required documents are combined with AND semantics.
Represents an individual governed rule within the Lexicon catalog (e.g. sold_back, sif_pif, person_deceased, daily_account_contact_limit_2).

Represents an immutable execution run of the Rule product, tracking run identity, execution mode, channel, and business date. Mutable lifecycle state (status, completion counts, timestamps) is captured via rule_execution_status_changed event edges.
Represents the top-level Rule product platform / engine (e.g. Gallade Rule engine).
Represents a governed ruleset configuration (e.g. communication-compliance-baseline, email-specific-rules, phone-interactions) grouping related rules.
Represents seller-provided identifiers used to match accounts with incoming media/documents.
Represents an immutable settlement offer record for a debt.
Represents a durable short URL artifact referenced by outbound debtor communications.

Represents a person's social security number in the graph as an immutable salted hash, and exposes external-only read projections (SSN last-four and full SSN) that are resolved from an approved operational source at read time and are never persisted to the graph.
Represents a durable communication or postal template definition whose authored content is stored in Git and referenced by messages or other channel-specific artifacts.

Represents an individual outbound or inbound text message (SMS/MMS). Linked to the person and debt it concerns via person_has_text_message and debt_has_text_message, to the phone number it was sent to / received from via phone_number_has_text_message, to call-triggered attribution via phone_number_has_call_triggered_text_message, to the template used to render outbound messages via text_message_rendered_from_template, to lifecycle status transitions via text_message_status_changed (self edges), to the durable short URL presented in the message via text_message_has_short_url, to the business treatment campaign it was sent under via text_message_has_campaign, and to the URI of its rendered artifact via text_message_has_rendered_artifact_uri. Replaces the prior edge-based `text_message` model.

Represents a single visit (one-time event) of a short URL. Each time a short URL is opened, a new trace vertex is created and linked from the short URL via the short_url_has_trace edge, so a short URL visited three times has three trace vertices linked to it.
Represents an immutable TU score enrichment associated with a person.

Represents immutable evidence of a signed unsubscribe link embedded in an outbound email. The live non-expiring URL and token are bearer opt-out credentials and are intentionally excluded; the exact URL remains protected inside the rendered email artifact linked from the email_message.
